reading.body:
Browser-use alone commands 111,940 stars, more than a third of the 287,709 total across all five repositories, making it the single dominant project in this open-source slice of the coding and browser agent space.

The five repositories split cleanly into two browser-control projects and three coding agents. All five are active, none archived, and the most recent pushes for four of them share the same date, suggesting sustained parallel development across both categories. The licence split, three Apache-2.0 and two MIT, means every project here permits commercial use, which lowers the barrier for teams embedding these agents into production pipelines.

For AI infrastructure, the relevance is indirect but real. Coding agents that autonomously write and test software compress the human time between a model capability and a deployed system, which accelerates the demand cycle for compute. Browser agents extend model reach to any web interface without requiring an API, multiplying the surface area over which inference runs. Neither connection is visible in star counts alone, and the data says nothing about inference volume, model size requirements, or the power load these tools generate when run at scale.
